667:
As used in this article, the following definitions apply:
Act means the Georgia Massage Therapy Practice Act, enacted by and defined in O.C.G.A. § 43-24A-1 et seq. as amended.
Board means the Georgia Board of Massage Therapy, enacted by the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 43-24A-4.
For hire means a reasonable expectation that the person to whom the massage is provided, or some third person on his or her behalf, will pay money, give other consideration, or provide any gratuity therefore.
Massage means the application of a system of structured touch, pressure, movement, and holding to the soft tissue of the body in which the primary intent is to enhance or restore health and well-being. The term includes complementary methods, including without limitation, the external application of water, superficial heat, superficial cold, lubricants, salt scrubs, or other topical preparations and the use of commercially available electromechanical devices which do not require the use of transcutaneous electrodes and which mimic or enhance the actions possible by the hands; the term also includes determining whether massage therapy is appropriate or contraindicated, or whether referral to another health care provider is appropriate. Massage therapy shall not include the use of ultrasound, fluidotherapy, laser, and other methods of deep thermal modalities.
Massage business or massage parlor means a business with a location in the city at which any person engages in or offers massage, regardless of the name of the business or the words used to describe the business through signage or advertisement or in filings with the secretary of state. Massage parlors are subject to regulation by a local government, pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-9(b)(17) and O.C.G.A. § 43-24A-22(a) as amended.
Massage therapist means:
(1) A person who holds a valid, current, unrevoked, and unsuspended state license in the practice of massage therapy issued by the board pursuant to the Georgia Massage Therapy Practice Act.
(2) A person who holds a valid, current, unrevoked, and unsuspended state provisional permit in the practice of massage therapy issued by the board pursuant to the Georgia Massage Therapy Practice Act, and working under the supervision of a licensed massage therapist.
(3) A person pursuing a course of study leading to a degree or certificate as a massage therapist in an educational program recognized by the board, if such person is designated by title indicating student status and is fulfilling uncompensated work experiences required for the attainment of the degree or certificate, and working under the supervision of a licensed massage therapist.
(4) A nonresident person rendering massage therapy up to sixty (60) days during a twelve-month period for treatment of a temporary sojourner only; provided that such nonresident massage therapist holds a license, registration or certification from another state, jurisdiction or country if the requirements as determined by the Georgia Board for Licensure are substantially equal to the requirements contained in this chapter; or provided that such nonresident massage therapist is currently nationally certified in therapeutic massage and bodywork.
(5) A person duly licensed, registered, or certified in another jurisdiction, state, territory, or a foreign country when incidentally in this state to provide service as part of an emergency response team working in conjunction with disaster relief officials or as part of a charity event with which he or she comes into the state.
Masseuse, masseur, massage practitioner, or persons practicing massage means a person who performs or engages in the practice of massage.
State license means a license to practice massage therapy issued by the board, pursuant to the Act.
(Ord. No. 10-16, § 1, 10-21-2010)

(a) State license. No person other than a massage therapist shall perform or offer to perform massage in the City of Dublin.

(1) Medical doctors and osteopaths, chiropractors, physical and occupational therapists, podiatrists, acupuncturists, registered or licensed practical nurses, barbers, beauty culturists, and cosmetologists duly licensed to practice in this state pursuant to O.C.G.A. tit. 43.
(2) Employees of duly licensed nursing and convalescent homes and hospitals while working at their place of employment.
(3) Athletic directors or trainers who are affiliated with an accredited educational institution or a bona fide sports team and whose work is limited to athletic team members.
(4) Any other individual or entity expressly exempted from local regulation of massage therapy by the laws of the state.
(5) A person who restricts his or her practice to the manipulation of the soft tissue of the human body to hands, feet, or ears who does not have the client disrobe and does not hold himself or herself out as a massage therapist.
(6) Any person who desires to provide in Dublin only certain bodywork services which the person believes are of a modality that is not a massage as defined in this article may request from the planning commission a waiver of the licensing requirements of this chapter for conducting the business of and providing such bodywork services. Such request will be made in writing, filed with the city clerk at least fifteen (15) days before the regularly scheduled meeting of the planning commission, and shall fully explain why the modality is not massage therapy. The planning commission shall act upon the request at the next regularly scheduled meeting. If the request is granted, the licensing requirements of this chapter shall be waived for the person making the request. The decision of the planning commission may be appealed pursuant to this Code of Ordinances or state law.
(Ord. No. 10-16, § 1, 10-21-2010)
682:
It is the purpose of this article to protect the public health, safety, and general welfare of individuals and the community at large; to establish uniform regulations for the operation of mobile food service units; and to enhance street-level economic opportunities within the city.
(Ord. No. 19-22, § 1, 11-7-2019)
683:
This article shall apply to the operation of all mobile food service units within the corporate limits of the city.
(Ord. No. 19-22, § 1, 11-7-2019)
684:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Base of operation means a food service establishment, or any other permitted location in which food, container, or supplies are kept, handled, prepared, packaged, stored, or placed in containers for subsequent transport, sale, or service elsewhere.
Fixed food service establishment means a non-mobile public or private establishment which prepares and serves meals, lunches, short orders, sandwiches, frozen desserts, or other edible products directly to the consumer either for carry out or service within the establishment. The term includes restaurants, coffee shops, cafeterias, short order cafes, luncheonettes, taverns, lunchrooms, places which retail sandwiches or salads, soda fountains, and similar facilities by whatever name called. This term shall not apply to establishments offering food service incidental to their operations, such as convenience stores, gas stations, and the like.
Food truck encompasses all mobile food service units with the exception of pushcarts.
Mobile food service unit means a trailer, pushcart, vehicle vendor or any other similar conveyance operating as an extension of an under the managerial authority of the permit holder of its permitted base of operation for the retail sale or distribution of food and/or beverage.
Pushcart means a human propelled, self-contained, enclosed food service cart that operates at pre-determined locations as approved by the health authority and the City of Dublin. Pushcarts shall be no larger than five (5) feet by ten (10) feet.
Ice cream truck means a food truck in which ice cream, popsicles, ice sherbets or other frozen desserts of any kind are carried for the purpose of retail sale on the streets of the city, but no other types of food.
(Ord. No. 19-22, § 1, 11-7-2019)
686:
Review and consideration of an application shall be conducted in accordance with principles of due process. Applications may be denied where an applicant fails to demonstrate that he or she meets the conditions and requirements of this article, or where an applicant fails to comply with applicable local, state, or federal law. Applications may be denied for any individual or entity that has a past due account balance of any kind with the city until such time as the past due amounts have been paid. Any false statements, material omissions or substantially misleading information provided in an application or furnished by an applicant in connection with an application constitute grounds for any one (1) or combination of the following sanctions: denial; refusal to renew; revocation; suspension; and imposition of penalties.
(Ord. No. 19-22, § 1, 11-7-2019)
687:
(a) Food trucks. The following operational requirements and conditions apply to food trucks:
(1) Food trucks shall not conduct business within the public right-of way, with the exception of special events recognized by the City of Dublin for which the food truck has received written pre-approval from the city manager.
(2) Food trucks shall not operate on private property without the written consent of the property owner.
(3) No operator or employee of a food truck may, at any time, utilized amplified sound devices.
(4) Food trucks shall comply with the city's grease interceptor standards, as set forth in chapter 24 of this Code of Ordinances, as amended.
(5) The Georgia Department of Public Health mobile food service unit permit, together with all applicable health certificates, including food inspection reports, pertaining to the unit, shall be firmly attached in a prominent location, which shall be plainly visible to the public at all times the food truck is conducting business.
(6) Any driver of a food truck must possess a valid driver's license.
(7) Food trucks may conduct business only within the permitted zones of the city in accordance with Appendix A of this Code of Ordinances, as amended.
(8) When conducting business, food trucks shall provide no less than nine (9) feet of unobstructed horizontal pedestrian clearance on private property, as measured from the main service window.
(9) Food trucks may not be left unattended or otherwise stored on sites at which they offer the sale of food and beverage to the public, unless authorized by the property owner or during a special event sanctioned by the city manager.
(10) Food trucks shall comply with all applicable local, state, and federal health and safety laws, regulations and rules.
(11) Food trucks may place on temporary sandwich board for advertisement purposes no more than four (4) feet from the main service window.
(12) Food trucks may not conduct business in a location that might block or impede either pedestrian or vehicle traffic.
(13) Food trucks may not conduct business with any person while such person is situated in a motor vehicle.
(14) Toilet facilities - See Georgia Department of Public Health Rule 511-6-1-.06(2)(h).
(15) Food trucks may not conduct business in such manner as to obstruct the view from any right-of-way of a business, public building, or any traffic control signal or sign.
(16) Temporary seating may be provided to patrons of food trucks, but must be stored and/or removed daily.
(b) Pushcarts. The following operational requirements and conditions apply to pushcarts:
(1) No operator or employee of a pushcart may, at any time, utilize amplified sound devices.
(2) No pushcart may be operated within the right-of-way nor within any public parking lot of the city.
(3) The Georgia Department of Public Health mobile food service unit permit, together with all applicable health certificates, including food inspection reports, pertaining to the unit, shall be firmly attached in a prominent location, which shall be plainly visible to the public at all times the pushcart is conducting business.
(4) Pushcarts may conduct business only within the permitted zones of the city in accordance with Appendix A of this Code of Ordinances, as amended.
(5) When conducting business, pushcarts shall provide no less than six (6) feet of unobstructed horizontal pedestrian clearance on private property, as measured from the main service window.
(6) Pushcarts shall comply with all applicable local, state, and federal health and safety laws, regulations, and rules.
(7) Pushcarts may not display signage not affixed to the vehicle or cart itself.
(8) Pushcarts may not conduct business in a location that might block or impede either pedestrian or vehicular traffic.
(9) Pushcarts may not conduct business with any person while such person is situated in a motor vehicle.
(10) Pushcarts may not furnish temporary seating.
(11) Pushcarts may not conduct business in such a manner as to block or obstruct the view from the right-of-way to any business, public building, or any traffic control or sign.
(12) Vendors operating from registered pushcarts are permitted to sell food and cut flowers only.
(c) Ice cream trucks. Ice cream trucks are subject to all of the provisions for food trucks, except they may conduct business in the public right-of-way of a residentially zoned areas of the city in accordance with Appendix A of this Code of Ordinances, but may not remain stationary in any residential neighborhood, except when actually serving customers. Ice cream trucks may operate within residentially zoned areas of the city in accordance with Appendix A of this Code of Ordinances only during the period between sunrise and sunset each day. Ice cream trucks may play music, as is customary for ice cream trucks, but only during daylight hours.
(Ord. No. 19-22, § 1, 11-7-2019; Ord. No. 20-05, § 6, 3-5-2020)
688:
(a) Each mobile food service unit shall provide a suitably sized receptacle for litter, which shall be located within ten (10) feet of the service window of the unit. It shall be maintained and regularly emptied. All waste generated by the mobile food service unit's operation, including that associated with its customer and staff, must be disposed of at the base of operation, or some other location where authorization has been given by the owner of that location.
(b) The area within which a mobile food service unit operates shall, at all times, be kept clean and free from litter, garbage, rubble, and debris. For purposes of this section, a mobile food service unit shall be responsible for maintaining in a safe and hygienic manner, the premise on which it is situated.
(c) The operator of a mobile food service unit may not dispose of wastewater at any location permitted herein, but shall remove the same and dispose of at the base of operation or other authorized location.
(Ord. No. 19-22, § 1, 11-7-2019)
689:
All mobile food service units subject to an occupation tax certificate issued by the city shall be inspected by the fire inspector annually and shall be in compliance with all applicable fire codes adopted by the City of Dublin to operate within the city limits of Dublin.
(Ord. No. 19-22, § 1, 11-7-2019; Ord. No. 26-02, § 1, 3-5-2026)
690:
The city manager may permit licensed mobile food service units to operate at special events pursuant to such policies and procedures he/she deems appropriate in consideration of the event in question. Special event permits are of a limited duration and not subject to the prohibitions set forth in subsections (a)(7) and (b)(4) of section 12-125.
(Ord. No. 19-22, § 1, 11-7-2019)
691:
As part of the permitting process set forth herein, any person or entity receiving a permit set forth herein shall execute an indemnity agreement indemnifying and releasing the City of Dublin, its agents, employees, and elected officials from any and all liability against any and all claims, actions, and suits of any type, whatsoever.
(Ord. No. 19-22, § 1, 11-7-2019)
692:
(a) To ensure the continued application of the intent and purpose of this article, the city manager shall notify the owner(s) and operator(s) and, where applicable, the Laurens County Health Department, of all instances in which a citation is issued to a mobile food service unit.
(b) The city manager shall maintain a record of all code violation charges, founded accusations, and convictions concerning mobile food service units. When a mobile food service unit owner or operator accumulates three (3) code violations for a particular mobile food service unit within a period of twelve (12) consecutive months, the city shall revoke the mobile food service unit's location approvals and reject all applications for mobile food service unit location approvals by the concerned owner(s) and operator(s) for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months following the date of revocation.
(c) If a mobile food service unit or operator has been cited for and found to be in violation of any zoning, health, or life safety code provision, the owner or operator must demonstrate compliance with the applicable code prior to being eligible to continue operations under the current approval.
(d) Violations of this article are subject to the following sanctions, which may not be waived or reduced, and which may be combined with any other legal remedy available to the city:
a. First violation: $500.00.
b. Second violation within the twelve (12) months following the first violation: $750.00.
c. Third violation within the twelve (12) months following the first violation: $1,000.00 and revocation of the mobile food service unit location approvals.
(e) Nothing in this section shall limit the city from enforcement of its code, state, or federal law by any other legal remedy available to the city. Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit or supplant the power of any city inspector, deputy marshal, or other duly empowered officer under the city's ordinances, rules, and regulations or the authority granted under state law, as amended, to take necessary action, consisted with the law, to protect the public from operation of a mobile food service unit as a nuisance, including abatement thereof by lawful means.
(f) Each day that a person operates as a mobile food service unit without complying with the provisions of this article constitutes a separate offense.
(g) This article may be enforced by the city tax marshal, code enforcement officer, or any law enforcement officer with the powers of arrest.
(Ord. No. 19-22, § 1, 11-7-2019)
695:
(a) Effective May 1, 2022, a recovery residence permit must be obtained from the city clerk to operate any recovery residence within the corporate limits of the City of Dublin, Georgia. Said permit shall be effective for one (1) year from the date of application. A new permit is required and new application for each year or part of any year a recovery residence operates. Facilities which meet the definition of a recovery residence, as defined herein, which are currently in operation shall have ninety (90) days from the effective date of this article to obtain the permit required herein or cease operation.
(b) The city clerk shall establish an application form which requires identifying information for the entity operating the facility; a primary point of contact for the facility; proof of the certification required herein, as well as attestation to compliance with the minimum standards as required herein. The city clerk shall also request any other information needed to ensure this article is given full effect. Prior to issuance of any permit herein, the city clerk shall verify the building has been inspected by a building inspector, fire inspector, or other designated personnel of the city and that all of the criteria required herein are met and satisfied.
(Ord. No. 22-10, § 2, 5-5-2022)
697:
All recovery residences shall affirm on the application for the permit required herein that they will adhere to and comply with and shall maintain the following minimum standards while in operation:
(a) The residence must be in good repair, clean, and well maintained while in operation; and
(b) Fifty (50) plus square feet of space shall be afforded per bed, per sleeping room; and
(c) A minimum of one (1) sink, toilet, and shower shall be available for every six (6) residents; and
(d) Each resident shall have personal item storage space available which is capable of being secured; and
(e) Each resident has personal food storage space available which is capable of being secured; and
(f) That laundry services are accessible to all residents; and
(g) All appliances are in safe, working condition; and
(h) A meeting space large enough to accommodate all residents is provided; and
(i) A comfortable group area is available to provide space for small groups and socializing; and
(j) The kitchen and dining areas are large enough to accommodate all residents for meals and meal preparation; and
(k) The residence has an annual safety inspection by the building inspector and/or fire inspector of the city which meets all of the life safety codes and the requirements herein; and
(l) An adopted policy regarding smoke-free living environment and/or designated smoking area outside the residence which is enforced; and
(m) Emergency numbers, procedures (including overdose and other emergency responses) and evacuation maps are posted in conspicuous locations throughout the recovery residence; and
(n) That resident rights, rules, responsibilities, schedules, emergency procedures, emergency numbers, staff contact numbers, and grievance process are posted in all residences and provided to all residents; and
(o) That resource directories, written or electronic, are made available to residents; and
(p) 24-hour surveillance cameras in all common areas and on the exterior of all entryways with the capability for a staff member, manager, or owner to view live footage or twenty-four-hour staff on site; and
(q) Require that residents be accompanied by a staff member if leaving the facility for any purpose other than work, counseling, or other program related activity.
(Ord. No. 22-10, § 2, 5-5-2022)
698:
No permit shall issue for any recovery residence which is proposed to be located within one thousand five hundred (1,500) feet of another permitted or operating recovery residence. Said distance shall be measured from the closest point of the property line where the recovery residence is located to the closest point of the nearest property line of any other property where a recovery residence is located. The city clerk shall maintain a list of all known recovery residences in the city for the purpose of complying with this section.
(Ord. No. 22-10, § 2, 5-5-2022)
699:
The following terms when used within this Article VI shall have the following meanings:
Building inspector means the individual identified in City Ordinance Section 6-26 of the City of Dublin Code of Ordinances or his or her designee.
City clerk means the clerk of the City of Dublin or his or her designee.
Fire inspector means the fire inspector of the City of Dublin as appointed by the Fire Chief.
Georgia Association of Recovery Residences means the non-profit organization of the same name based out of Atlanta, Georgia.
National Alliance for Recovery Residences means the non-profit organization of the same name based out of St. Paul, Minnesota.
Recovery residence means any occupation or business which provides a sober, safe, and/or healthy living environment that promotes recovery from alcohol, drug use, or any associated problem.
(Ord. No. 22-10, § 2, 5-5-2022)
700:
(1) Any person violating any provision of this article or who operates a recovery residence without a valid permit may be summoned to appear before the Municipal Court of the City of Dublin, and upon conviction be guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), or imprisonment for not more than sixty (60) days, or both.
(2) The city clerk or building inspector may bring an appropriate action in the appropriate court of law to enforce the provisions of this article, including, but not limited to, injunctive relieve to prohibit continued violation of this article.
(Ord. No. 22-10, § 2, 5-5-2022)
703:
This article shall be known as the "Vape Shops Ordinance of the City of Dublin, Georgia."
(Ord. No. 25-03, § 1, 5-22-2025)
704:
For the purposes of this ordinance:
"Vape shop" shall mean any retail establishment where 25% or more of the floor space, inventory, or gross revenue is derived from the sale, display, or distribution of vapor products, including but not limited to electronic cigarettes, vape pens, e-liquids, or related accessories.
"Vapor product" shall mean any consumable vapor product or vapor device as defined by O.C.G.A. § 48-11-1(17) and (39), including any liquid solution or device intended to deliver nicotine or other substances via inhalation of an aerosol.
(Ord. No. 25-03, § 1, 5-22-2025)
705:
(a) No new vape shop shall be established, permitted, operated or licensed within the corporate limits of the City of Dublin after the effective date of this ordinance.
(b) This prohibition applies to the issuance of new occupational tax certificates, zoning approvals, and any other permits required for the operation of a vape shop.
(Ord. No. 25-03, § 1, 5-22-2025)
706:
(a) Any vape shop lawfully operating within the City of Dublin as of the effective date of this ordinance, with a valid occupational tax certificate issued pursuant to the Dublin Code of Ordinances, shall be permitted to continue operation as a nonconforming use.
(b) Such grandfathered status shall terminate if:

(2) The ownership of the vape shop changes;

(c) Grandfathered vape shops must comply with all existing and future state laws (e.g., O.C.G.A. § 16-12-171) and local regulations regarding the sale of vapor products.
(Ord. No. 25-03, § 1, 5-22-2025)
707:
(a) Violation of this ordinance shall be punishable as provided in section 1-10 and 1-11 of the Dublin Code of Ordinances and/or revocation of applicable licenses or permits.
(b) The city manager or his designee is authorized to enforce this ordinance, including inspections to verify compliance.
(Ord. No. 25-03, § 1, 5-22-2025)
708:

710:
For the purposes of this chapter, the following words shall have the meanings respectively ascribed below:
Nuisance: Anything which causes hurt, inconvenience or damage to another provided that the hurt, inconvenience or damage complained of shall not be fanciful, or such as would affect only one of fastidious taste, but rather such as would affect an ordinary, reasonable man; and the fact that the act done may otherwise be lawful shall not keep it from being a nuisance.
Nuisance per se: An act, occupation or structure which is a nuisance at all times and under any circumstances, regardless of location or surroundings.
Private nuisance: A nuisance limited in its injurious effect to one or a few individuals.
Public nuisance: A nuisance which damages all persons who come within the sphere of its operation, though it may vary in its effects on individuals.
711:
(a) The various nuisances described and enumerated in this section shall not be deemed to be exclusive, and this section shall not be construed to limit the broad definitions of nuisance found in section 13-1 above, but shall be in addition to all other nuisances described and prohibited in this Code.
(b) The following are hereby declared to be nuisances:
(1) Things interfering with peace or comfort: Sounds, animals or things that interfere with the peace or comfort or disturb the quiet of the community.
(2) Obnoxious and offensive odors: The emission of obnoxious and offensive odors; the tainting of the air rendering it offensive or unwholesome so as to affect the health or comfort of reasonable persons residing in the neighborhood thereof.
(3) Discharging of offensive matter: The placing or throwing or discharging from any house or premises and flow from or out of any house or premises of any filthy, foul or offensive matter or liquid of any kind into any street, alley or public place or upon any adjacent lot or ground.
(4) Water pollution: The obstruction or pollution of any watercourse or source of water supply in the city.
(5) Stagnant water: Standing and stagnant water on the premises.
(6) Emission of dense smoke: The emission of dense smoke from any fire, chimney, engine, oil burner or other agency in the city so as to cause disturbance or discomfort to the public. For the purpose of testing and grading the density of smoke, the Ringelmann Smoke Chart as published and used by the United States Geological Survey shall be the standard for such grading, and smoke shall be defined and declared to be dense when it is of a degree of density of number three on the chart, or greater, for more than six (6) minutes in any one (1) hour, whether such period of time is consecutive or not.
(7) Vacant lots: Any vacant lot whereon debris is permitted to accumulate and remain, or where brush and grasses are permitted to grow, in such a manner as to create a fire hazard or other hazard to the public health, safety and welfare.
(8) Nonconforming structures, machines, etc: Any building, business, thing, machine or machinery erected, repaired, conducted, maintained, operated or used contrary to or in violation of any of the fire and safety regulations of this Code, state law or city ordinance, and any improvement that is an unsafe structure as defined in article III of this chapter.
(9) Animal enclosures: Any enclosure in which any animals are kept, dog kennels or runs and other animal or fowl pens wherein manure, dung, filth, vermin or litter is allowed to accumulate.
(10) Dead animals: The carcass of any dead animal of any kind on any premises within the city.
(11) Depositing trash, garbage, and refuse on private or public property: The depositing and leaving on private or public property of trash, garbage, refuse, scrap building materials, paper, cardboard containers, brick, cement rubbish, tree residue, cans, containers or any other rubbish or trash that is a menace to public health and safety in the city or which unreasonably annoys others.
(12) Unoccupied buildings: Unoccupied buildings that are not properly painted, cleaned, and secured.
(13) Unsafe vehicles, machinery, etc.: Unsheltered storage of old, unused, stripped, or junked vehicles, machinery, implements, and/or equipment and personal property of any kind that is no longer safely usable for the purposes for which it was manufactured for a period of thirty (30) days or more, except in licensed junkyards. The absence of a license plate for the current year and/or the absence of a current motor vehicle registration shall be prima facie evidence that such vehicle is junked.
(14) Gutters or spouts: Any gutter or spout that conveys filth into any city street, lane or alley.
(15) Statutory nuisances: Any other condition constituting a nuisance under other sections of the Code of Ordinances, City of Dublin, or state law, including state minimum standard codes, building, fire, life and safety codes.
(Ord. No. 89-14, 9-21-89; Ord. No. 05-16, §§ I, II, 11-10-2005)
712:
It shall be unlawful for any person to maintain or permit the existence of any nuisance on any property within the city. Violations of this section shall be punishable by imprisonment not to exceed one (1) year, a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), or both for each offense. Each day a nuisance continues to exist is a separate offense.
(Ord. No. 05-16, 11-10-2005)
713:
Whenever any nuisance exists within the city or whenever any condition shall exist on any property within the city that is required or subject to be demolished, removed or abated under this article or any other city ordinance the chief of police, the chief building inspector or their designees may issue a summons and cause the summons to be served upon such owner or other person responsible for the condition. The summons shall describe the condition complained of and specify the ordinances or parts thereof claimed to be violated thereby. The summons shall require such person to appear before the municipal judge at a time, date and place specified therein, to show cause why such condition should not be demolished, removed or abated.
(Ord. No. 05-16, 11-10-2005)
714:
(a) If the court at the hearing required by section 13-4 shall determine that a condition does exist as alleged that constitutes a nuisance or a condition which under this Code or the city ordinances is required or subject to be demolished, removed or abated, the judge shall issue his order and judgment so finding. The order may provide any or all of the following:
(1) That the property owner or other person responsible therefor shall demolish, remove or abate the condition within a period of time to be fixed by the judge.
(2) How the condition is to be abated, including but not limited to rehabilitation or demolition of any buildings or structures located on the property in question.
(3) That if the property owner or other person responsible therefor shall fail to comply with the order within the time specified, the city shall be authorized to proceed without further notice to demolish, remove or abate such condition and to take whatever action is deemed necessary to demolish, remove or abate such condition.
(4) Fine or imprisonment within the parameters of section 13-3.
(b) The expense thereof, including court costs and attorney fees, shall be charged against the owner of the property in question and shall be a lien against the property upon which the condition existed, ranking equally with the lien for city taxes. Execution shall issue for such costs as for city taxes, and the procedure for the enforcement of the execution shall thereafter be the same as for city taxes.
(c) Should the judge find that it is in the best interest of justice, he may order the city to proceed with a nuisance abatement action under article III of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 05-16, 11-10-2005)
715:
Whenever any condition shall exist which constitutes an immediate and grave hazard to public health and safety requiring immediate action, the condition may be abated or otherwise remedied summarily and without following the procedures set forth herein. Notice shall be given to the owner or manager responsible for the property of a hearing to be held at the next scheduled court date of the Dublin City Court.
(Ord. No. 05-16, 11-10-2005)
716:
Whenever it shall be necessary for the city to proceed under sections 13-4 and 13-5 and the owner of the property or other person responsible therefor resides outside the city limits or cannot be found after diligent search, service of the notice required by section 30-75 shall be made by:
(1) Mailing a copy of the notice to any known address, by certified or registered mail or by statutory overnight mail;
(2) Posting a copy of the notice on the property involved; and
(3) Publishing the notice in a newspaper having general circulation in the city once a week for four (4) consecutive weeks, the last notice to be not longer than ten (10) days nor less than one (1) day prior to the hearing. When personal service cannot be made upon such person within the city limits, the case shall proceed as quasi in rem, and the execution shall issue in rem.
(Ord. No. 05-16, 11-10-2005)
717:
Nothing in this article shall in any way affect the power and authority of the municipal judge to punish for any other violations, which the conditions may constitute, nor shall it affect the power and authority of the judge to punish by contempt the failure to comply with his order.
(Ord. No. 05-16, 11-10-2005)

720:
It shall be unlawful for any person to abandon any vehicle or appliance of any type within the city nor shall any vehicle or appliance left at any place within the city for such time and under such circumstances as to cause such vehicle or appliance reasonably to appear to have been abandoned.
(Ord. No. 69-9, § 1, 4-21-69)
721:
It shall be unlawful for any person to leave any partially dismantled, nonoperating, wrecked or junked vehicle or appliance on any street, lane or highway within the city.
(Ord. No. 69-9, § 2, 4-21-69)
722:
It shall be unlawful for any person in charge or control of any property within the city, whether as owner, tenant, occupant, lessee or agent thereof, to permit or allow any partially dismantled, nonoperating, wrecked, junked or discarded vehicle or appliance of any kind or character to remain on such property within the city longer than fifteen (15) days unless said vehicle is stored in an enclosed building or located on the premises of a business enterprise operated in a lawful place or manner, when necessary to the operation of such business enterprise, or such vehicle or appliance is stored in an appropriate place and maintained in a lawful manner.
(Ord. No. 69-9, § 3, 4-21-69)

(Ord, No. 69-9, § 4, 4-21-69)
724:

745:
For purposes of this Code section, the following terms are defined as follows:
Direct light: Light emitted directly from the lamp, off of the reflector or reflector diffuser, or through the refractor or diffuser lens, of a luminaire.
Fixture: The assembly that houses the lamp(s) and can include all or some of the following parts: A housing, a mounting bracket or pole socket, a lamp holder, a ballast, a reflector or mirror, and/or a refractor or lens.
Glare: Light emitting from a luminaire with an intensity great enough to reduce a viewer's ability to see (and in extreme cases causing momentary blindness), or that causes annoyance or discomfort.
Indirect light: Direct light that has been reflected or has scattered off of other surfaces.
Light trespass: The shining of light produced by a luminaire beyond the boundaries of the property on which it is located.
Luminaire: A complete lighting system, including a lamp or lamps and a fixture. This term shall be interpreted broadly as applying to all outdoor electrically powered illuminating devices, outdoor lighting or reflective surfaces, lamps and similar devices (permanently installed or portable), used for illumination or advertisement.
Luminaire, full cutoff: Outdoor light fixtures shielded or constructed so that no direct light rays are emitted by the installed fixture at angles above the horizontal plane.
Outdoor lighting: The night-time illumination of an outside area or object by any manmade device located outdoors that produces light by any means.
Searchlight: High-intensity electric light with a reflector shaped to concentrate the beam, used to illuminate or search for distant objects or as a beacon.
Security lighting: Exterior lighting installed solely to enhance the security of people and property by aiding detecting and deterring intruders.
(Ord. No. 09-07, 5-7-2009)

(a) A person commits the offense of loitering when he is in a place at a time or in a manner not usual for law-abiding individuals, under circumstances that warrant a justifiable and reasonable alarm or immediate concern for the safety of persons or property in the vicinity.

(a) Purpose and findings. The mayor and council do hereby find and declare that:
(1) It is the intent of the mayor and council in enacting this section to recognize free speech rights for all citizens while at the same time protecting the coexistent rights for all citizens to enjoy safe and convenient travel in public spaces free from intimidating conduct, threats, and harassment that stem from certain types of abusive solicitation, or that may give rise to interference with other's activities if they occur in particular settings and contexts; and
(2) There are numerous forms of solicitation that are not in and of themselves inherently threatening or aggressive, including vocal request for a donation; carrying or displaying sign requesting donations; shaking or jingling a cup of change; and ringing a bell in compliance with the city's noise ordinance; and
(3) There has been an increase in aggressive solicitation in the city, which threatens the security, privacy, and freedom of movement of both residents and visitors; and
(4) The presence of solicitors in certain specific areas (such as near to or adjacent to automatic teller machines, adjacent to outside seating areas, and in public parking lots) create reasonable concerns by citizens objectively worried about their privacy, freedom of movement, and personal security; and
(5) Certain forms of solicitation impede the orderly flow of pedestrian and vehicular traffic and leads to concerns regarding traffic and public safety, particularly in congested roadways and sidewalks (as defined below to include highly traveled areas, lines to enter buildings, commercial districts with narrow sidewalks or on small traffic medians of high-speed or high-volume streets and highways); and
(6) It is not the intent of the mayor and council or this section to limit an individual's right to exercise free speech associated with solicitation; rather it aims to impose specific time, place, and manner restrictions on solicitation and associated conduct in certain limited circumstances; namely, limiting aggressive panhandling, panhandling at locations or times deemed particularly threatening and dangerous, and panhandling in places where people are a "captive audience" and there is a wish to avoid or reduce a threat of inescapable confrontations; and
(7) In promulgating this section, the mayor and council seek to impose regulations that are narrowly tailored to serve the aforementioned significant governmental interests.
(b) Definitions. The following terms or phrases when used within this section shall have the meanings set forth below:
(1) "Aggressive begging, panhandling, or solicitation" includes the following forms of conduct:
a. Confronting someone in a way that would cause a reasonable person to fear bodily harm;
b. Accosting an individual by approaching or speaking to the individual or individuals in such a manner as would cause a reasonable person to fear imminent bodily harm or the commission of a criminal act upon his or her person, or upon property in his or her immediate possession;
c. Touching someone without his or her consent;
d. Using obscene, profane, or abusive language toward someone while attempting to panhandle or solicit him or her;
e. Forcing oneself upon the company of another by engaging in any of the following conduct:
i. Continuing to solicit in close proximity to the individual addressed after the person to whom the solicitation is directed has made a negative response, either verbally, by physical sign, by attempting to leave the presence of the person soliciting, or by other negative indication that the individual addressed does not desire to be solicited;
ii. Blocking the passage of the individual solicited; or
iii. Otherwise engaging in conduct that could reasonably be construed as intending to compel or force a person to accede to a solicitation; or
f. Acting with the intent to intimidate someone into giving money; or
g. Other conduct that a reasonable person being solicited would regard as threatening or intimidating in order to solicit a contribution or donation.
(2) "Areas with heightened personal security concerns" include the following locations:
a. Areas within, or within twenty (20) feet of, a public parking lot between dusk and dawn;
b. Areas within twenty (20) feet of a public bus stop between dusk and dawn;
c. Areas within twenty (20) feet of access to building entrances, public event venues, public accommodations or commercial businesses;
d. Areas within a designated commercial district in which a high volume of pedestrian traffic or narrow sidewalks and streets give a reasonable person a justified, reasonable concern about his or her personal security due to congestion and close proximity to others, including, but not limited to, the sidewalks facing Jackson Street, any and all public alleyways, the pedestrian plaza area which runs from West Jackson Street to the public parking lot located behind the buildings fronting West Jackson Street; or the Bicentennial Plaza.
e. Other areas in which congestion would give a reasonable person a reasonable, justified concern for his or her personal security due to congestion and close proximity to others.
(3) "Areas with heightened personal privacy concerns" include the following:
a. Locations within twenty (20) feet of an automated teller machine, or financial institution in which an automatic teller machine is located, where "financial institution" means any bank, credit union, or finance company;
b. Locations within twenty (20) feet of a restaurant outdoor seating area during operating hours unless the solicitor's presence is authorized by the proprietor; or
c. Other locations in which a reasonable person would have a reasonable and justified concern about whether congestion and close proximity to others could compromise his or her interest in privacy.
(4) "Areas with heightened public safety concerns" include the following:
a. Streets or highways;
b. Traffic medians where such medians provide less than eight (8) square feet of flat space for standing; or
c. Traffic medians of whatever size within designated high traffic roadways or high-speed roadways.
(5) "Begging, panhandling, and charitable or political solicitation" includes the following activities: actions that are conducted in the furtherance of the purpose of immediately collecting contributions for the use of one's self or others. As used in this section, the word "solicit" and its forms, includes requests for funding arising from begging, panhandling, charitable, or political fundraising initiatives. "Begging, panhandling, and charitable or political solicitation" also includes both "aggressive" and "passive" forms of begging panhandling and charitable or political solicitation, but these forms are regulated separately under this section.

(9) "Passive panhandling, begging, charitable or political solicitation" means conduct that falls within the definition in subsection (5) of this section, but only such conduct that involves requests for contributions presented in writing without speaking, oral request for contributions that do not constitute "aggressive panhandling, begging, charitable or political solicitation" or other activities that do not fall within the definition of "aggressive begging, panhandling, or solicitation" as defined in subsection (1) of this section.
(c) Passive begging, panhandling, charitable or political solicitation. When regulated passive panhandling, begging, charitable or political solicitation permitted except where expressly prohibited.
The mayor and council find that passive panhandling, begging, charitable or political solicitation, as defined in subsection (b)(9) of this section should be treated as speech protected under the First Amendment to the United States Constitution unless other well-grounded governmental concerns are implicated. Accordingly, passive panhandling, begging, charitable or political solicitation is permitted throughout the corporate limits of the City of Dublin except as prohibited in subsections (e) and (f) of this section.
(d) Aggressive panhandling, begging, charitable and political solicitation prohibited.
(1) No person shall engage in aggressive panhandling, begging, charitable or political solicitation as defined in subsection (b)(1) of this section at any time or at any location within the City of Dublin.
(2) Any person who violates this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by up to twelve (12) months' confinement and one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) fine.
(e) Regulation of panhandling, begging, charitable and political solicitation in areas with specific personal safety and privacy concerns.
(1) Regulated Locations: Both "passive" and "aggressive" panhandling, begging, charitable and political solicitation activities are regulated in the following areas that give rise to specific personal safety and privacy concerns as defined in subsection (b) of this section:
a. Areas with heightened personal security concerns as previously defined in subsection (b)(2); and
b. Areas with heightened personal privacy concerns as previously defined in subsection (b)(3).
(2) Prohibition. Neither "aggressive" nor "passive" panhandling, begging, charitable and political solicitation shall be conducted in areas defined as involving heightened personal security or heightened privacy concerns.
(3) Any person who violates this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by up to twelve (12) months' confinement and one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) fine.
(f) Panhandling, begging, charitable and political solicitation and protection of public access and vehicular safety in public streets and highways and on traffic medians and on high volume and high-speed highways.
(1) Areas regulated. Areas regulated by this section include those defined as areas with heightened public safety concerns as defined in section (b)(4) of this section.
(2) Findings. The mayor and council find as follows:
a. Both aggressive and passive begging, panhandling, charitable or political solicitation within streets and highway rights-of-way, or on small traffic medians (less than eight (8) linear feet between the two (2) lanes of travel), or on traffic medians located on high speed and high-volume traffic corridors as identified in this section, give rise to an increased risk of injury to solicitors on medians, traffic congestion, and traffic accidents that may affect drivers or solicitors;
b. This section provides ample alternative sites for passive begging, panhandling, charitable and political solicitation in areas that do not give rise to enhanced public safety concerns or personal privacy and security concerns; and
c. Evidence. The city manager and city staff have undertaken to consider and identify areas in which small traffic medians may put solicitors or motorists at risk, and high speed and high volume traffic corridors that likewise are especially dangerous, in order to assure that those regulations are grounded in appropriate governmental concerns, are narrowly tailored, and allow alternative avenues for communication and in developing this section.
(3) Prohibitions:
a. Generally. Both passive and aggressive begging, panhandling, charitable or political solicitation shall be prohibited in "areas with heightened public safety concerns" as defined in subsection (b)(4).
b. Exceptions. The mayor and council may identify limited periods each year in which these prohibitions as they relate to passive begging, panhandling, charitable or political solicitation should not be enforced as a result of particularly pressing governmental concerns related to such activities.
i. Charitable initiatives. Mayor and council may designate up to ten (10) days a year as days on which these prohibitions shall not apply in order to allow effective solicitation for designated charities, provided that appropriate safety measures are implemented, and a permit issued by the police chief.
ii. Election activities. The council may designate up to five (5) days a year on which these prohibitions shall not apply in order to allow effective political communications in connection with local, state, and federal elections, provided that appropriate safety measures are implemented.
iii. Documented public safety plan. In the event that the mayor and council designate days as exceptions from this section's requirements, it shall also adopt a documented public safety plan to reduce risks to public safety that might otherwise arise.
iv. Comparable treatment. To the extent that the mayor and council adopt exceptions to the prohibitions set forth in section (f)(3)(a), relating to charitable initiatives and election activities, such exceptions shall extend to all parties otherwise covered by the provisions of this section relating to begging, panhandling, charitable, and political solicitation.
(g) Penalties. Violators shall be subject to the maximum penalties provided by law.

782:
The following acts are declared to be loud, disturbing and unnecessary noises in violation of this article, but said enumeration shall not be deemed to be exhaustive:
(1) Motor vehicle horns: The sounding of any horn on any automobile, motorcycle or other motor vehicle on any street or public place of the city except as a warning signal.
(2) Radios, television sets and similar devices: The using, operating or permitting to be played, used or operated, any radio receiving set, musical instrument, phonograph, television set or other machine or device for the producing or reproducing of sound between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. in such manner as to disturb the peace, quiet and comfort of neighboring residents.
(3) Loudspeakers and amplifiers: The using or operating of any loudspeaker or sound-amplifying device mounted upon any vehicle within the city for the purpose of broadcasting or advertising any information about any business or activity for any other purpose, unless a permit for such sound amplification has been obtained from the city manager or chief of police.
(4) Construction equipment and activity: The operating of any equipment or the performing of any outside construction or repair work on buildings, structures, roads or projects within the city between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. unless a permit for such construction or repair work between such hours has been obtained from the city manager or chief of police.
(5) Exhausts: The discharging into the open air of the exhaust of any internal combustion engine, motorboat or motor vehicle except through a muffler or other device which will effectively prevent loud or explosive noises therefrom.
(6) Animals and birds: The keeping of any animal or bird which by frequent or continuous barking, chirping or other means of communication disturbs the comfort or repose of the residents of any residential neighborhood.
(7) Vehicle repair in residential areas: The repairing, rebuilding or testing of any motor vehicle between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. within any residential area in such a manner as to disturb the peace, quiet and comfort of the residents of the area.
(8) Schools, courts, churches, hospitals: The creating of any excessive noise on any street adjacent to any school, institution of learning, church or court while the same are in use, or adjacent to any hospital, which unreasonably interferes with the workings of such institution or which disturbs or unduly annoys patients in the hospital, provided conspicuous signs are displayed in such streets indicating that the same is a school, hospital or court street.
(9) Hawkers and peddlers: The selling of anything by outcry within the residential areas of the city, except at licensed sporting events, parades, fairs, circuses and other similar licensed public entertainment events.
(10) Drums: The using of any drum or other instrument or device for the purpose of attracting attention by the creation of noise within the city, unless a permit for such use has been obtained from the city manager or chief of police.

(b) The board shall consist of seven (7) members who shall be appointed by the mayor with the consent of the City Council of the City of Dublin,
Georgia, and who shall be residents of Laurens County, but need not be residents of the City of Dublin, Georgia. The board shall choose its own officers and keep minutes of all proceedings. A majority of the members present shall be a quorum for the transaction of business. Appropriate city staff as determined by the city manager shall assist and advise the board, and the board shall be authorized to engage third parties for technical assistance as needed.

(Ord. No. 23-14, § 2, 10-19-2023)

(Ord. No. 23-14, § 2, 10-19-2023)

a) Activities approved or permitted by the city manager, or any of the city's authorities or agencies as to their respective properties, shall be exempt from these requirements.

(a) The violation of any rule provided herein governing the use of any park is unlawful and a misdemeanor offense punishable as provided in section 1-10 of the Code.

(14) No children under the age of twelve (12) are allowed in the area without close adult supervision.
(15) No food of any kind, human or dog, including dog treats, is allowed.
(16) No feeding of dogs.

The planning commission shall consist of seven (7) members.

880:
(a) The members of the planning commission shall be appointed by the mayor, by and with the consent of the board of aldermen. All members who have served on said commission shall be eligible for reappointment to succeed themselves. The term of any member of the commission in office on the effective date of this section, and the term of any member appointed to the commission prior to the first regular meeting of the mayor and council to be held in January, 1979, shall expire upon the appointment and qualification of a successor.
(b) At the first regular meeting of the mayor and council held in January, 1979, the seven (7) members of the planning commission shall be appointed or reappointed for terms as set forth in section 17-19.

881:
At the first regular meeting of the mayor and council held in January, 1979, all seven (7) members of the planning commission shall be appointed or reappointed for initial terms of one, two (2) and three (3) years. At the time of appointment, at the first meeting of the mayor and council in January of 1979, two (2) members shall be appointed for one year; two (2) members shall be appointed for two (2) years; and three (3) members shall be appointed for three (3) years. Thereafter, the terms of all members shall be three (3) years.
(Code 1964, § 20-7; Ord. No. 78-20, § 1, 7-3-78)
882: Vacancies occurring in the membership of the planning commission shall be filled by appointments for unexpired terms only and in the same manner as for original appointments.
883: Any member of the planning commission may be removed by the mayor or city council for cause after written notice and a public hearing.
884: All members of the municipal planning commission shall serve without compensation.
885: The planning commission shall elect one of its members as chairperson who shall serve for one year or until such person is reelected or a successor is elected. A second appointive member shall be elected as vice-chairperson and shall serve for one year or until such person is reelected or a successor is elected. The commission shall appoint a secretary, who may be an officer or employee of the city or of the planning commission.
886: The planning commission shall meet at least once each month at the call of the chairperson and at such other times as the chairperson or commission shall determine.
887: The rules, regulations, and provisions contained in Chapter 69-12 of the Georgia Code Annotated governing the creation, appointment, organization, powers, and duties of municipal and county planning commissions are hereby adopted as the rules, regulations, and provisions governing the planning commission of this municipality.
888: The planning commission shall keep a record of its proceedings, which record shall be open to public inspection.
889: Employees and staff may be appointed by the planning commission as necessary.

893:
For the purposes of this chapter, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them as follows:
Dealer in precious metals and gems means any person, whether as owner, agent or employee, who engages in the business of purchasing precious metals or gems or articles containing any precious metal or gems from members of the general public for resale to brokers, dealers or melters.
Electronic reporting system means a computer based system as specified by the Chief of Police which is designed to record and transmit data and information electronically.
Gems means any precious or semiprecious stone which is cut and polished.
Goods means every species of tangible personal property.
Pawnbroker means any person (with the exception of title pawnbrokers), whether as owner, agent or employee, engaged in whole or in part in the business of lending money on the security of pledged goods, or in the business of purchasing tangible personal property on the condition that it may be redeemed or repurchased by the seller for a fixed price within a fixed period of time, or in the business of purchasing tangible personal property from persons or sources other than manufacturers or licensed dealers as a part of or in conjunction with the business activities described in this section.
Pawnshop means any person (with the exception of title pawnbrokers), whether as owner, agent or employee engaged in whole or in part in the business of lending money on the security of pledged goods, or in the business of purchasing tangible personal property on the condition that it may be redeemed or repurchased by the seller for a fixed price within a fixed period of time, or in the business of purchasing tangible personal property from persons or sources other than manufacturers or licensed dealers as a part of or in conjunction with the business activities described in this section.
Person means an individual, partnership, corporation, joint venture, trust, association, or other legal entity however organized.
Precious metals means metals that are considered rare or having a high economic value including, but not limited to, silver, gold, platinum and similar metals and their alloys.
(Ord. No. 81-3, § 1, 2-5-81; Ord. No. 15-05, § 1, 5-21-2015)
894:

(Ord. No. 81-3, § 2, 2-5-81; Ord. No. 15-05, § 1, 5-21-2015)
895:
(a) No person shall engage in business as a dealer in precious metals and gems in the city except under a license granted by the city.
(b) A license for a dealer in precious metals and gems shall authorize the licensee to engage in the business of a dealer in precious metals and gems as defined herein.
(c) Application for a license shall be made to the city clerk.
(d) All applications for a license shall require a fee as set by resolution and on file at the office of the city clerk. All applications shall be in writing upon a form supplied to all applicants by the clerk. The application shall be made by a person having at least a twenty-five (25) percent ownership interest in the business and shall set forth the names, addresses and ages of all persons having an ownership interest in the business and shall contain an accurate description of the premises upon which the business is to be conducted, along with the zoning classification therefor and such other information as may be required.
(e) All applicants shall swear or affirm that the information disclosed in the application is true and correct.
(f) The license application must be approved by the chief of police and accompanied by a report from the office of the chief of police indicating that the police department has made an investigation of all persons identified on the application as having an ownership interest in the business and that said investigation has not revealed any felony convictions or convictions for violation of any laws or ordinances involving larceny, burglary or theft of any description as defined in Title 26 of Georgia Code Annotated. A plea of guilty or nolo contendere or a bond forfeiture shall be considered a conviction for the purposes of this subsection.
(Ord. No. 81-3, § 3, 2-5-81; Ord. No. 15-05, § 1, 5-21-2015; Ord. No. 25-12, § 34, 9-18-2025)
896:
(a) Every person having an ownership interest in the business carried on by a dealer in precious metals and gems and all employees engaged in said business shall be at least eighteen (18) years of age.
(b) Persons engaged in the business of purchasing gems, precious metals or goods made from precious metals shall not purchase gems, precious metals or goods made from precious metals from any person who has not provided positive identification, including reliable proof that such person is at least eighteen (18) years of age.
(Ord. No. 81-3, § 4, 2-5-81; Ord. No. 15-05, § 1, 5-21-2015)
897:
Every person or business engaged as a pawnbroker, pawnshop, and dealer in precious metals and gems within the City of Dublin shall secure from every person from whom he receives any goods, whether by purchase or through pledge, trade, pawn or exchange, the following:
(1) Government-issued photo identification card, such as a driver's license, military identification card, state identification card or passport;
(2) The name, address, telephone number, race, sex, height, weight, date of birth, and a social security or driver's license number;
(3) A digital photograph clearly showing a frontal view of the subject's face for each transaction, and if multiple transactions are made at different times of the same day a separate photo shall be taken. Each digital image shall be labeled with the date and time of the transaction and stored in such a manner that they are safe from corruption; a video surveillance system that records and stores the information set forth above shall be deemed to comply with the requirements of this subsection;
(4) A complete and accurate description of the goods acquired, including the following information, if available:
(a) Brand name.
(b) Model number.
(c) Manufacturer's serial number.
(d) Color, as apparent to the untrained eye.
(e) Precious metal type, weight, and content if known.
(f) Gemstone description.
(g) In the case of firearms, the type of action, caliber or gauge.
(h) Any other unique identifying marks, numbers, or letters.
(i) The date and time of the transaction.
(j) For jewelry and gems, a digital photograph of the goods acquired.
(5) The pawnbroker, pawnshop and dealer in precious metals and gems shall maintain the above information and digital photographs for a period of three (3) years and make the same available to law enforcement personnel upon request.
(6) The pawnbroker, pawnshop and dealer in precious metals and gems shall require the seller to sign a statement verifying that the seller is the rightful owner of the goods or is entitled to sell, consign, or trade the goods.
(Ord. No. 81-3, § 5, 2-5-81; Ord. No. 15-05, § 1, 5-21-2015; Ord. No. 15-09, § 1, 10-15-2015)
898:
Every pawnbroker, pawnshop and dealer in precious metals and gems located within the City of Dublin shall make a computer-generated daily report, in such format as prescribed by the City of Dublin Police Department, of all transactions that occurred during the twenty-four-hour period ending at 9:00 p.m. on the date of the report. A report shall be made each day prior to 11:59 p.m. for each day the operator or dealer transacts business. Daily reports shall be filed electronically by posting to a law enforcement web site designated by the police department. Where technological problems prevent posting the daily report electronically, a printed, typed or legibly handwritten report shall be delivered to the police department in lieu thereof.
(Ord. No. 15-05, § 1, 5-21-2015)
899:
(a) Any pawnbroker, pawnshop or dealer in precious metals and gems who takes goods on pawn, taking full title thereto, shall hold the goods so taken in pawn for at least thirty (30) days before disposing of the goods by sale, transfer, shipment or otherwise.
(b) Any pawnbroker, pawnshop or dealer in precious metals and gems who buys goods, taking full title thereto shall hold the goods so taken in on purchase for at least ten (10) days before disposing of the goods by sale, transfer, shipment or otherwise, and shall not alter the original form, shape or condition of such metals during the ten-day holding period.
(c) The City of Dublin Police Department or any other law enforcement agency has the authority to place property that is the subject of a law enforcement investigation on law enforcement hold. In that event, the Dublin Police Department or other law enforcement agency shall notify the pawnbroker, pawnshop, secondhand dealer, or dealer in precious metals and gems of the need for a law enforcement hold and identify all property subject to the law enforcement hold. Upon notification, it shall be the responsibility of the pawnbroker, pawnshop or dealer in precious metals and gems to maintain the subject property until such time as the property is released from law enforcement hold status or the property is confiscated as evidence.
(Ord. No. 81-3, § 6, 2-5-81; Ord. No. 15-05, § 1, 5-21-2015)
900:
Licenses issued pursuant to this chapter shall be subject to revocation or suspension by the mayor and council, after reasonable notice and an opportunity to be heard has been given to a licensee. If the city manager has determined that there is probably cause to believe that a licensee or an employee of a licensee has violated this chapter, the city manager may temporarily suspend said license for a period not to exceed fifteen (15) days.
(Ord. No. 81-3, § 7, 2-5-81; Ord. No. 15-05, § 1, 5-21-2015)
901:
(a) The City of Dublin finds that pawnbrokers, pawnshops and dealers in precious metals and gems are engaged in a business that is a pervasively regulated industry and that proper enforcement of this article requires the administrative inspection of the commercial property where these businesses are located.
(b) All goods pledged or sold to a pawnbroker, pawnshop and dealer in precious metals and gems as well as all records and documentation required to be kept by this article shall be subject to an administrative inspection by the Dublin Police Department as provided for in this article.
(c) As such, every pawnbroker, pawnshop and dealer in precious metals and gems shall admit to his premises, without a search warrant, any police officer, or designated civilian employee of the City of Dublin Police Department, whose duties include verifying compliance with the requirements of this article and locating goods that are missing or stolen. These administrative inspections shall occur during normal business hours unless consented to by the pawnbroker, pawnshop and dealer in precious metals and gems.
(Ord. No. 15-05, § 1, 5-21-2015)
902:

These inspections shall be made for the purpose of verifying compliance with the requirements of this article and to locate goods that are missing or stolen. 908:
(a) Except as otherwise provided in section 17½-23, the scrap metal processor, owner, keeper, proprietor, collector, or dealer of any scrap metal shall hold the scrap metal purchased separate and apart from all other materials purchased for a period of not less than seven (7) working days after the date of purchase, during which period the scrap metal processor, owner, keeper, proprietor, collector, or dealer shall not change the form of the scrap metal and shall permit any law enforcement officer to make inspection of the scrap metal.
(b) However, any transaction for the purchase of a scrap metal wherein a digital photographic record, video record, or other record format is used to clearly identify the seller and the scrap metal that the seller is selling shall be exempt from this holding requirement. 917:
It shall be the duty of all railroad companies to keep the street crossings over their tracks level with the tops of the rails by planks or otherwise, and in a safe and convenient condition for vehicles and pedestrians. When the railroad runs under any street so as to make a bridge necessary, it shall be the duty of said company to keep such bridge safe and in good repair at all times. They shall also keep their water conductors sound and large so as to carry off and leave no standing water. Upon failure of any railroad company to comply with this section the agent of said company shall be served with a notice of the defect and, upon the failure to comply herewith within five (5) days, the same shall be remedied by the city at the expense of the company and the costs collected by execution against the company as provided in case of a nuisance. 923:
Those members of the board of education of the City of Dublin who are serving as such on December 31, 1992, and any person selected to fill a vacancy in any such offices shall continue to serve as such members for terms of office which expire December 31, 1993. On and after January 1, 1994, the board of education of the city, shall consist of seven (7) members of whom four (4) shall be elected from education districts described in section 19-17 below; two (2) of whom shall be elected from super-districts described in section 19-17; and one (1) of whom shall be elected at large.
(Ord. No. 93-1, § 2(a), 2-4-93)
924:
(a) For purposes of electing members of the board of education, the City of Dublin School District is divided into four (4) education districts. One (1) member of the board shall be elected from each such district. Those districts shall consist of the following described territory of the city school districts:
Education District 1
Education District 2
Education District 3
Education District 4
One (1) member of the board shall be elected from each super-district, with Super-District I being comprised of Education District 1 and Education District 2 and Super-District II being comprised of Education District 3 and Education District 4. One (1) member of the board shall be elected at large.
(b) For purposes of Georgia Laws 1993, Act No. 6, Section 2(b):
(1) The terms "tract," "block," and "VTD" shall mean and describe the same geographical boundaries as provided in the report of the bureau of the census for the United States decennial census of 1990 for the State or Georgia;
(2) The term "precinct" is synonymous with the term "voting precinct" and means a geographical area designated by O.C.G.A. Title 21, Chapter 2, Article 7, with which all electors vote at one (1) polling place;
(3) Whenever the description of any education district refers to a named city, it shall mean the geographical boundaries of that city as shown on the census map for the United States decennial census of 1990 or subsequent years for the State of Georgia;
(4) Precinct names and designations following VTD designations are included for convenience only; and in the event the description of any education district contains a conflict between the geographical boundaries of any VTD and the boundaries of the following named precinct, the geographical boundary of the VTD as shown on the census maps for the United States decennial census of 1990 or subsequent years for the State of Georgia shall control;
(5) Any part of the City of Dublin school district which is not included in any education district described in Georgia Laws 1993, Act No. 6, Section 2(b) shall be included within that education district contiguous to such part which contains the least population according to the United States decennial census of 1990 or subsequent years for the State of Georgia; and
(6) Any part of the City of Dublin school district which is described in Georgia Laws 1993, Act No. 6, Section 2(b) as being included in a particular education district shall nevertheless not be included within such education district if such part is not contiguous to such education district. Such noncontiguous part shall instead be included within that education district contiguous to such part which contains the least population according to the United States decennial census of 1990 or subsequent years for the State of Georgia.
(Ord. No. 93-1, § 2(b),(c), 2-4-93)

925:
(a) No person shall be a member of the board if that person is ineligible for such office pursuant to Code Section 45-2-1 of the O.C.G.A. or any other general law.
(b) In order to be elected as a member of the board from an education district, a person must have resided in that district for at least six (6) months immediately prior to qualifying for election thereto; have reached the age of twenty-one (21) years; possess a high school diploma or its equivalency; and must receive a plurality of the votes cast for that office in that district only and not at large. Only electors who are residents of the education district may vote for a member of the board for that district. At the time of qualifying for election as a member of the board from an education district, each candidate for such office shall specify the education district for which that person is a candidate. A person elected as a member of the board from an education district must continue to reside in that district during that person's term of office or that office shall thereupon become vacant.
(c) In order to be elected as a member of the board from Super-District I, a person must have resided in Super-District I for at least six (6) months immediately prior to qualifying for election thereto; have reached the age of twenty-one (21) years; possess a high school diploma or its equivalency; and must receive a plurality of the votes cast for that office in Super-District I only and not at large. Only electors who are residents of Super-District I may vote for a member of the board for Super-District I. At the time of qualifying for election as a member of the board from Super-District I, each candidate for such office shall specify the Super-District for which that person is a candidate. The member of the board who is elected from Super-District I may reside anywhere within the first or second education districts and must receive a plurality of the votes cast for such office in the first and second education districts. The member of the board from Super-District I must continue to reside within the first or second school district during that person's term of office or that office shall thereupon become vacant.
(d) In order to be elected as a member of the board from Super-District II, a person must have resided in Super-District II for at least six (6) months prior to qualifying for election thereto; have reached the age of twenty-one (21) years; possess a high school diploma or its equivalency; and must receive a plurality of the votes cast for that office in Super-District II only and not at large. Only electors who are residents of Super-District II may vote for a member of the board for Super-District II. At the time of qualifying for election as a member of the board from Super-District II, each candidate for such office shall specify the Super-District for which that person is a candidate. The member of the board who is elected from Super-District II may reside anywhere within the third and fourth education districts and must receive a plurality of the votes cast for such office in the third and fourth education districts. The member of the board from Super-District II must continue to reside within the third and fourth education districts during that person's term of office or that office shall thereupon become vacant.
(e) In order to be elected a member of the board for the at-large post, a person must have resided within the city limits of Dublin for at least six (6) months prior to qualifying for election thereto; have reached the age of twenty-one (21) years; possess a high school diploma or its equivalency; and, must receive a plurality of the votes cast for that office city-wide. All electors of the City of Dublin may vote for the member of the board running for the at-large post. At the time of qualifying for election as an at-large member of the board, each candidate must specify he is qualifying for the at-large post. The board member elected at large may reside anywhere in the city and must receive a plurality of the votes cast for said office. The at-large member must continue to reside in the city during that person's term of office or that office shall thereupon be vacant.
(Ord. No. 93-1, § 3, 2-4-93)
926:

Those members of the board elected thereto from Education Districts Nos. 1, 2, 3, and 4 in 1993 shall take office the first day in January immediately following that election and shall serve for initial terms of office which expire December 31, 1995, and upon the election and qualification of their respective successors.
